explanation: Entering the war was Democratic policy, and it was contested. Much of the army, part of the Evolutionists, and most of the country outside Lisbon had no wish to fight. The majority won in June 1915 is what let the Democrats carry the policy out. A Democratic government seized the seventy-odd German ships in Portuguese harbours in February 1916 at Britain’s request, and Germany declared war a fortnight later. The claim here is narrow. The election did not cause the declaration, and the government that provoked it could not have been formed without the June result.
